groups.name: Industrial Systems
groups.summary: Systems for production, physical assets, maintenance, quality, materials and plant operations.
groups.introduction: Industrial systems support the work carried out in factories, process facilities, utilities and other operational environments. Their scope can include production planning and execution, asset management, maintenance, quality, laboratory operations, materials and plant data. The right system boundary depends on the process, equipment structure and level of operational traceability required.

subgroups.name: Production & Planning
subgroups.description: Planning resources and capacity, defining products, and recording production execution.

subgroups.name: Asset & Maintenance
subgroups.description: Maintaining asset registers, managing work orders, and analysing equipment condition and reliability.

subgroups.name: Quality, Laboratory & Safety
subgroups.description: Managing quality controls, laboratory testing, risk, safety and compliance records.

subgroups.name: Warehouse & Materials
subgroups.description: Controlling inventory and the physical movement of materials.

subgroups.name: Plant Data & Energy
subgroups.description: Collecting equipment data, maintaining process history and analysing energy use.

seo.title: Industrial Systems
seo.description: Systems for production, physical assets, maintenance, quality, materials and plant operations.

groups.name: Business Systems
groups.summary: Systems for procurement, suppliers, customers, orders and connected supply chains.
groups.introduction: Business systems structure the commercial processes that connect an organisation with suppliers, customers and partners. They can support sourcing, purchasing, supplier relationships, sales, order management and logistics. Their value depends on clear process ownership, reliable master data and well-defined links with finance and operational systems.

subgroups.name: Procurement & Sourcing
subgroups.description: Managing purchasing processes, supplier selection, contracts and procurement information.

subgroups.name: Supply Chain & Logistics
subgroups.description: Coordinating supply, transport, inventory and distribution activities.

subgroups.name: Sales & Commerce
subgroups.description: Supporting customer relationships, commercial offers, orders and digital channels.

seo.title: Business Systems
seo.description: Systems for procurement, suppliers, customers, orders and connected supply chains.

groups.name: Enterprise Systems
groups.summary: Systems for people, finance, projects, IT, governance and internal services.
groups.introduction: Enterprise systems support the internal management of an organisation. Their scope can include people and workforce processes, financial planning, project management, IT services, identity, governance, records and facilities. Clear responsibilities and consistent information are important where processes cross departments.

subgroups.name: People & Workforce
subgroups.description: Managing employee information, recruitment, payroll, workforce planning and learning.

subgroups.name: Finance & Project Management
subgroups.description: Supporting financial planning, project delivery and portfolio oversight.

subgroups.name: IT & Digital Workplace
subgroups.description: Managing IT services, technology assets, identities and access.

subgroups.name: Governance, Process & Information
subgroups.description: Managing enterprise processes, records, controls, audit and information.

subgroups.name: Facilities & Workplace
subgroups.description: Coordinating buildings, spaces, workplace services and facility operations.

seo.title: Enterprise Systems
seo.description: Systems for people, finance, projects, IT, governance and internal services.

groups.name: Data, Analytics & Integration
groups.summary: Systems for connecting, managing, contextualising and analysing business and operational data.
groups.introduction: Data and analytics systems bring information from industrial, business and enterprise applications into a more consistent context. Depending on the need, they can support integration, master data, operational data, reporting, analytics and process insight. Data ownership, quality, timeliness and governance should be defined before selecting the architecture.

subgroups.name: Data Management & Integration
subgroups.description: Connecting systems and managing shared, operational and analytical data.

subgroups.name: Analytics & Intelligence
subgroups.description: Turning operational and business data into reporting, analysis and decision support.

seo.title: Data, Analytics & Integration
seo.description: Systems for connecting, managing, contextualising and analysing business and operational data.

products.name: Enterprise Resource Planning
products.shortDescription: One integrated system for finance, accounting, procurement, sales, inventory, human resources, and production.
products.definition: ERP coordinates the core resources and processes of an organisation through a shared data model. Orders, purchasing, stock, production and finance use consistent records across different roles. Its scope is typically aligned with the organisation’s operating model, production processes and commercial requirements.
products.problem: When purchasing, sales, stock, production and accounting live in separate tools, records never quite match and true product cost is hard to calculate.
capabilities: General ledger, accounting, and cost accounting
Inventory, bills of materials, and costing
Production orders, routings, and material consumption
workflow: Set up organisation structure and master data
Record orders, purchases and operational events

distinctions.text: ERP coordinates the organisation's transactions and resources. MES records what actually happens on the production floor, in detail.

faqs.question: Does ERP replace MES?
faqs.answer: No. ERP coordinates resources and transactions across the organisation; MES records production order execution, actual consumption and line events.

seo.title: AIMS Core – Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
seo.description: One integrated system for finance, accounting, procurement, sales, inventory, human resources, and production.

products.name: Computerized Maintenance Management System
products.shortDescription: Maintenance requests, work orders, preventive schedules, inspections, technicians, and spare parts in one system.
products.definition: A CMMS turns maintenance from reactive firefighting into planned, recorded work. Every request, inspection, and repair is linked to the equipment it concerns, so the history of each asset builds up automatically and cost and downtime become visible.
products.problem: Scattered requests and irregular schedules make it hard to prioritise repairs or to follow cost and downtime.
capabilities: Maintenance requests and work order management
Preventive maintenance by calendar, meter, or condition
Technician assignment, labour, and time recording
Maintenance history, cost, and downtime analysis
workflow: Prioritise and plan the work order
Carry out the work and record the result
Close the order and update the history

distinctions.text: CMMS focuses on work orders and maintenance activity. EAM covers the wider asset record and lifecycle.

faqs.question: What data is needed to start with a CMMS?
faqs.answer: An equipment and location list, failure history, service schedules, failure codes, technicians and spare-part information are the main inputs.

seo.title: AIMS Maintain – Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS)
seo.description: Maintenance requests, work orders, preventive schedules, inspections, technicians, and spare parts in one system.

products.name: Enterprise Asset Management
products.shortDescription: Manage physical assets across their full lifecycle: acquisition, operation, maintenance, performance, and retirement.
products.definition: EAM extends maintenance into a complete view of the asset base. It records what each asset is, where it is, what it has cost, and how it performs, so decisions about repair, renewal, and investment rest on evidence.
products.problem: Without an asset record and lifecycle history, decisions about repair, replacement and investment rest on incomplete data.
capabilities: Hierarchical asset register with locations and classes
Lifecycle records from acquisition to disposal
Cost tracking: purchase, maintenance, and total cost of ownership
workflow: Register the asset and its location
Record acquisition, installation and status changes

distinctions.text: EAM manages the asset across its lifecycle. CMMS handles maintenance requests and work orders.

faqs.question: Is EAM the same as CMMS?
faqs.answer: No. A CMMS centres on maintenance work. EAM adds the asset record, criticality, cost and lifecycle on top of maintenance.

seo.title: AIMS Assets – Enterprise Asset Management (EAM)
seo.description: Manage physical assets across their full lifecycle: acquisition, operation, maintenance, performance, and retirement.

products.name: Manufacturing Execution System
products.shortDescription: Connect production planning to shop-floor execution by tracking orders, materials, batches, and performance as work happens.
products.definition: MES is the layer between the plan and the machines. It releases production orders to the floor, records what is actually made and consumed, and reports progress and losses in real time so supervisors can act while there is still time.
products.problem: The gap between plan and actual execution limits timely visibility of progress, material use, scrap and stoppages.
capabilities: Production order release and dispatch to work centres
Material consumption and batch or lot recording
Genealogy and traceability from material to product
Live production status and shift reporting

distinctions.text: ERP manages orders and resources. MES records how each order is actually executed on the floor.

faqs.question: What does MES capture that ERP does not?
faqs.answer: Detail of order execution on the floor: operations performed, actual consumption, stoppages, scrap and traceability.

seo.title: AIMS Production – Manufacturing Execution System (MES)
seo.description: Connect production planning to shop-floor execution by tracking orders, materials, batches, and performance as work happens.

products.name: Warehouse Management System
products.shortDescription: Control receiving, put-away, storage, picking, packing, dispatch, and stock movement by location.
products.definition: WMS gives every unit of stock a location and every movement a record. Warehouse staff follow directed tasks, counts stay accurate, and dispatch is fast because the system knows where each item is.
products.problem: Stock recorded only at warehouse level does not show where items are or the status of each stock unit.
capabilities: Location and bin management with zones
Receiving against purchase orders with quality hold
Batch, lot, serial, and expiry tracking
workflow: Put away to a defined location

distinctions.text: SCM coordinates the flow of the supply chain. WMS manages physical operations and stock inside the warehouse.

faqs.question: Does every warehouse need a WMS?
faqs.answer: It depends on the number of locations, the volume of goods movement, traceability needs and how complex operations are.

seo.title: AIMS Warehouse – Warehouse Management System (WMS)
seo.description: Control receiving, put-away, storage, picking, packing, dispatch, and stock movement by location.

products.name: Quality Management System
products.shortDescription: Inspections, quality plans, non-conformities, corrective and preventive actions, audits, and quality records.
products.definition: QMS makes quality a managed process instead of a collection of forms. Inspections are planned and recorded, problems are logged as non-conformities, and corrective actions are tracked until they are verified closed.
products.problem: When inspections, results, non-conformances and corrective actions are kept apart, following a problem through to its cause is hard.
capabilities: Inspection plans and checklists for incoming, in-process, and final control
workflow: Carry out inspections and record results
Investigate the cause and set corrective action

distinctions.text: QMS manages quality processes and non-conformances. LIMS records samples and laboratory tests in detail.

faqs.question: How are non-conformances followed up in a QMS?
faqs.answer: By recording the source and description, investigating the cause, assigning actions and owners, and checking effectiveness before closing the case.

seo.title: AIMS Quality – Quality Management System (QMS)
seo.description: Inspections, quality plans, non-conformities, corrective and preventive actions, audits, and quality records.

products.name: Environment, Health and Safety
products.shortDescription: Workplace safety, environmental management, incident reporting, inspections, risk assessment, and permit-to-work.
products.definition: EHS brings safety and environmental obligations into the daily workflow. Incidents are reported where they happen, risks are assessed and controlled, hazardous work is authorised through permits, and corrective actions are followed through.
products.problem: Incidents and risk assessments recorded in different places make it hard to follow hazards, responsibilities and required controls.
capabilities: Incident and near-miss reporting with investigation
Corrective action tracking and safety reporting

distinctions.text: EHS focuses on safety and environmental risk. QMS focuses on product and process quality.

faqs.question: Does EHS replace environmental monitoring?
faqs.answer: No. EHS manages workflows and records. Receiving monitoring data depends on the data source and the integration design.

seo.title: AIMS Safety – Environment, Health and Safety (EHS)
seo.description: Workplace safety, environmental management, incident reporting, inspections, risk assessment, and permit-to-work.

products.name: Advanced Planning and Scheduling
products.shortDescription: Production schedules built from real capacity, material availability, constraints, and delivery requirements.
products.definition: APS turns demand into a schedule that can actually be executed. It considers machines, tooling, labour, and materials together, shows the consequences of changes, and helps planners commit to delivery dates they can keep.
products.problem: Planning against nominal capacity does not show the real effect of constraints on materials, tooling and labour.
capabilities: Constraint handling for tooling, labour, and material
What-if scenarios for rush orders and breakdowns
Delivery date promising and order loading
Schedule visualisation and release to production

distinctions.text: APS calculates the production plan. MES records actual operations and how far the plan was met.

faqs.question: When is APS worth considering?
faqs.answer: When capacity limits, operation sequences or delivery dates make manual planning difficult and the master data can be relied on.

seo.title: AIMS Planner – Advanced Planning and Scheduling (APS)
seo.description: Production schedules built from real capacity, material availability, constraints, and delivery requirements.

products.name: Laboratory Information Management System
products.shortDescription: Laboratory samples, test requests, methods, results, instruments, and workflows in one controlled system.
products.definition: LIMS replaces notebooks and spreadsheets with a structured record of every sample from receipt to reported result. Methods, specifications, and instruments are managed centrally, and results are checked against limits as they are entered.
products.problem: Scattered samples and results make it hard to trace a sample's path or link a result to its method and instrument.
capabilities: Sample registration, labelling, and chain of custody
Result entry with limit checking and review
workflow: Issue reports and keep the record

distinctions.text: LIMS manages samples and tests. QMS uses the results and evidence to manage quality.

faqs.question: What makes sample traceability possible?
faqs.answer: A sample ID, time and place of receipt, chain of custody, test method, instrument, responsible people and result version.

seo.title: AIMS Lab – Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
seo.description: Laboratory samples, test requests, methods, results, instruments, and workflows in one controlled system.

products.name: Energy Management System
products.shortDescription: Monitor and optimise energy consumption, utility cost, and efficiency across facilities and equipment.
products.definition: EMS shows where energy goes and what it costs. Metered consumption is collected by site, line, and machine, compared with production, and analysed to find waste, so efficiency work targets the biggest opportunities.
products.problem: Without combining meter readings and relating them to production and tariffs, it is hard to see where high consumption comes from.
capabilities: Metering and consumption collection by site and equipment
Energy per unit of production indicators
workflow: Aggregate consumption by site and equipment
connects: Meters and building or plant systems

distinctions.text: EMS manages consumption and energy indicators. Industrial analytics looks at energy data alongside production, quality and maintenance.

faqs.question: Does an EMS guarantee lower consumption?
faqs.answer: No. It makes consumption visible and analysable. Improvement depends on acting on what it shows and measuring the effect.

seo.title: AIMS Energy – Energy Management System (EMS)
seo.description: Monitor and optimise energy consumption, utility cost, and efficiency across facilities and equipment.

products.name: Product Lifecycle Management
products.shortDescription: Product definitions, engineering data, revisions, technical documents, and engineering change processes.
products.definition: PLM keeps engineering knowledge about products in one controlled place. Product structures, specifications, drawings, and revisions are managed with formal change approval, so production, purchasing, and quality always work from the current definition.
products.problem: Different versions of drawings and specifications can leave engineering, purchasing, production and quality out of step.
capabilities: Product and part master data with structures
Release of approved data to production and purchasing
workflow: Define the product and its engineering structure

distinctions.text: PLM controls engineering data and product change. DMS handles general document storage and retrieval.

faqs.question: How is PLM different from DMS?
faqs.answer: PLM manages product structure, engineering data and the change process. DMS focuses on registering and versioning documents.

seo.title: AIMS Lifecycle – Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
seo.description: Product definitions, engineering data, revisions, technical documents, and engineering change processes.

products.name: Industrial Monitoring and IIoT
products.shortDescription: Collect and present operational data from sensors, machines, control systems, and connected equipment on the web.
products.definition: This product brings equipment data into a web application where operations and maintenance can use it. Gateways collect readings over standard protocols, and the platform provides live views, alarms, and history without replacing the control layer.
products.problem: Equipment data sits in different sources and protocols, and is hard to use until it is collected and put in context.
capabilities: Data collection through gateways using standard industrial protocols
Live dashboards by site, line, and machine
Threshold and rule-based alarms and notifications
Hand-off of alarms to maintenance workflows
workflow: Pass data to monitoring and analysis

distinctions.text: IIoT focuses on connecting to equipment and collecting data. A historian stores time-series data for historical retrieval.

faqs.question: Can any equipment be connected?
faqs.answer: It depends on the protocol, controller, network access, security and the quality of the source data, and has to be checked for the target equipment.

seo.title: AIMS Sense – Industrial Monitoring and IIoT (IIoT)
seo.description: Collect and present operational data from sensors, machines, control systems, and connected equipment on the web.

products.name: Industrial Historian
products.shortDescription: Collect, store, and retrieve time-series data from industrial equipment and control systems.
products.definition: A historian is the long-term memory of the plant. It stores process values and events efficiently, keeps them available for years, and lets engineers compare periods, investigate incidents, and feed analytics with trustworthy data.
products.problem: Process data without timestamps and a retention policy cannot be relied on for incident analysis or trend comparison.
capabilities: Tag management with units, ranges, and quality flags
workflow: Retain data under the agreed policy

distinctions.text: A historian is specialised for industrial time-series data. An operational data platform puts a wider range of sources and data types in context.

faqs.question: How is a historian different from an ordinary database?
faqs.answer: It is designed to record and retrieve industrial time-series data with defined timestamps and sampling rates.

seo.title: AIMS Historian – Industrial Historian
seo.description: Collect, store, and retrieve time-series data from industrial equipment and control systems.

products.name: Asset Performance Management
products.shortDescription: Use condition, reliability, and operating data to find performance problems and improve asset availability.
products.definition: APM moves maintenance from fixed intervals to evidence. It combines failure history, condition readings, and operating context to rank asset risk, point to recurring failures, and focus maintenance effort where it prevents the most loss.
products.problem: Repair history alone does not say how likely a failure is. Asset criticality and equipment condition matter too.
capabilities: Asset health scoring from condition and failure data

distinctions.text: APM analyses asset condition and risk. CMMS plans and executes work orders.

faqs.question: Does APM predict failures with certainty?
faqs.answer: No. APM supports risk assessment and prioritisation. The accuracy of the analysis depends on the data and the model being sound.

seo.title: AIMS Reliability – Asset Performance Management (APM)
seo.description: Use condition, reliability, and operating data to find performance problems and improve asset availability.

products.name: E-Procurement
products.shortDescription: Purchase requests, internal approvals, purchasing policies, purchase orders, and procurement workflows.
products.definition: E-Procurement moves purchasing from email and paper into a controlled workflow. Requests are raised against budgets and policies, approved by the right people, and converted into purchase orders that suppliers can act on.
products.problem: Purchase requests travel by different routes, which makes it hard to control budgets and approval authority.
capabilities: Purchase requisitions with budget and policy checks
Purchasing reports by department, category, and supplier
workflow: Convert the request into an order

distinctions.text: E-Procurement controls requests and purchase orders. E-Sourcing manages competition and supplier selection.

faqs.question: Does e-procurement cover supplier selection?
faqs.answer: It can cover part of it. Competitive sourcing and bid evaluation usually belong to E-Sourcing.

seo.title: AIMS Procure – E-Procurement
seo.description: Purchase requests, internal approvals, purchasing policies, purchase orders, and procurement workflows.

products.name: E-Sourcing
products.shortDescription: Supplier discovery, sourcing events, tenders, requests for information and proposals, and supplier selection.
products.definition: E-Sourcing structures how an organization finds and selects suppliers. Sourcing events are run as defined processes with criteria, deadlines, and evaluation, which makes decisions comparable and defensible.
products.problem: Different bid formats and irregular timelines make fair comparison and a documented choice difficult.
capabilities: Tenders, RFIs, and RFPs with attachments and deadlines
workflow: Record the choice and pass on the result

distinctions.text: RFQ covers collecting and comparing prices. E-Sourcing has a wider scope for competition and evaluation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between e-sourcing and RFQ?
faqs.answer: An RFQ is a defined event for collecting prices. E-Sourcing can cover the whole competitive and evaluation process.

seo.title: AIMS Source – E-Sourcing
seo.description: Supplier discovery, sourcing events, tenders, requests for information and proposals, and supplier selection.

products.name: RFQ Management Platform
products.shortDescription: Create and distribute requests for quotation, collect supplier bids, compare offers, and record award decisions.
products.definition: The RFQ platform runs the quotation cycle end to end. A request is created once, sent to the right suppliers through the channels they use, and answers come back into a structured comparison instead of scattered messages.
products.problem: If specifications and terms are not identical across suppliers, prices and conditions cannot be compared properly.
capabilities: RFQ creation from requisitions or templates
Distribution to selected suppliers through multiple channels
Structured bid collection with line-level pricing
Side-by-side comparison with commercial and technical criteria
Award decisions with a full audit trail

distinctions.text: RFQ manages price requests. E-Sourcing covers the broader sourcing process.

faqs.question: How are quotations made comparable?
faqs.answer: By standardising specifications, units, delivery terms, quote validity and evaluation rules.

seo.title: AIMS Tender – RFQ Management Platform (RFQ)
seo.description: Create and distribute requests for quotation, collect supplier bids, compare offers, and record award decisions.

products.name: Supplier Relationship Management
products.shortDescription: Supplier onboarding, qualification, evaluation, performance tracking, documents, and ongoing relationships.
products.definition: SRM keeps a single, current record of every supplier and how they perform. Onboarding and qualification are structured, documents are tracked to expiry, and performance scores inform who is invited to bid next time.
products.problem: Documents, evaluations and performance records for suppliers end up scattered across departments.
capabilities: Performance metrics from delivery and quality data
Issue, audit, and corrective action tracking

distinctions.text: SRM manages the supplier record and performance. The portal is the channel for interaction and information exchange.

faqs.question: Is SRM just a supplier list?
faqs.answer: No. Beyond basic data it covers qualification, documents, performance evaluation and improvement actions.

seo.title: AIMS Suppliers – Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)
seo.description: Supplier onboarding, qualification, evaluation, performance tracking, documents, and ongoing relationships.

products.name: Supplier Portal
products.shortDescription: A workspace for suppliers to handle quotations, orders, documents, delivery updates, and communication.
products.definition: The portal gives suppliers one place to work with you. They receive requests, submit quotations, confirm orders, update deliveries, and share documents, while the team sees the same live status.
products.problem: Exchanging email and files leaves the status of inquiries, orders, documents and deliveries unclear to both sides.
capabilities: Secure supplier accounts with role-based access
Purchase order confirmation and change handling

distinctions.text: The portal is the supplier's point of interaction. SRM keeps the internal evaluation and relationship logic.

faqs.question: What should the portal show?
faqs.answer: Only what is needed for the supplier's role and interaction: inquiries, orders, documents and delivery status.

seo.title: AIMS Vendor – Supplier Portal
seo.description: A workspace for suppliers to handle quotations, orders, documents, delivery updates, and communication.

products.name: Contract Lifecycle Management
products.shortDescription: Contract creation, negotiation, review, approval, execution, renewal, and expiry in one managed process.
products.definition: CLM treats a contract as a managed asset. Drafts come from approved templates, reviews and approvals are tracked, obligations and dates are recorded, and renewals are raised before they lapse.
products.problem: Contract versions and amendments are scattered, making it hard to follow clauses, approvals, obligations and renewals.
workflow: Register the request and contract template

distinctions.text: CLM manages the contract lifecycle and obligations. DMS controls the repository and document versions.

faqs.question: How is CLM different from a contract folder?
faqs.answer: CLM manages the workflow, clauses, approvals and obligations. A document repository only stores files.

seo.title: AIMS Contracts – Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM)
seo.description: Contract creation, negotiation, review, approval, execution, renewal, and expiry in one managed process.

products.name: Spend Management
products.shortDescription: Visibility into organizational spending, purchasing patterns, budgets, and cost-control opportunities.
products.definition: Spend Management shows where money actually goes. Purchasing data is consolidated and classified, compared with budgets, and analysed by supplier, category, and cost centre to reveal duplicated buying, price variance, and savings opportunities.
products.problem: Different classifications of purchase and payment data make spend analysis by category and supplier difficult.
capabilities: Spend consolidation from purchasing and finance data
Price variance and contract compliance analysis

distinctions.text: Spend management analyses purchasing patterns. EPM covers wider budgeting and financial performance.

faqs.question: Does spend analysis guarantee savings?
faqs.answer: No. It reveals opportunities. Realising savings depends on decisions and action.

seo.title: AIMS Spend – Spend Management
seo.description: Visibility into organizational spending, purchasing patterns, budgets, and cost-control opportunities.

products.name: Supply Chain Management
products.shortDescription: Coordinate sourcing, supply planning, procurement, inventory, logistics, and supplier operations.
products.definition: SCM gives planners one view from supplier to customer. Demand, stock, open orders, and lead times are combined so shortages and excess are seen early, and replenishment decisions are made on data instead of habit.
products.problem: When sourcing, purchasing, inventory and shipping decisions are made separately, matching supply to demand is hard.
capabilities: Supplier lead time and reliability monitoring

distinctions.text: SCM coordinates the supply chain as a whole. TMS manages execution of transport and shipments.

faqs.question: Does SCM replace WMS and TMS?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. SCM covers broad coordination across the chain. WMS and TMS are specialised for warehousing and transport.

seo.title: AIMS Supply – Supply Chain Management (SCM)
seo.description: Coordinate sourcing, supply planning, procurement, inventory, logistics, and supplier operations.

products.name: Transportation Management System
products.shortDescription: Plan and manage freight, carriers, shipments, transport costs, and delivery execution.
products.definition: TMS turns shipments into planned, tracked movements. Loads are planned, carriers are assigned and monitored, costs are recorded per shipment, and delivery status is visible to both the team and the customers.
products.problem: Transport planning and the tracking of shipment cost and status happen in separate channels.
capabilities: Shipment tracking and proof of delivery
workflow: Record the load and shipping details
Plan the route and assign a carrier

distinctions.text: TMS manages transport between origin and destination. WMS covers the movement of stock inside the warehouse.

faqs.question: What information is needed to track a shipment?
faqs.answer: Shipment ID, origin and destination, type of load, carrier, schedule, route events and proof of delivery.

seo.title: AIMS Transport – Transportation Management System (TMS)
seo.description: Plan and manage freight, carriers, shipments, transport costs, and delivery execution.

products.name: Customer Relationship Management
products.shortDescription: Customers, leads, opportunities, sales activities, and every interaction in one record.
products.definition: CRM gives the sales and service team a shared memory of each customer. Leads move through a defined pipeline, activities and conversations are logged, and management sees forecasts built from real opportunities.
products.problem: Customer information and sales opportunities spread across people and tools, so continuity of the relationship suffers.
workflow: Assess the need and create an opportunity
Record the outcome and pass to order

distinctions.text: CRM manages the relationship and sales opportunity. OMS follows a confirmed order through supply and delivery.

faqs.question: How is CRM different from OMS?
faqs.answer: CRM manages interaction and opportunity before the sale. OMS follows order fulfilment after the order is placed.

seo.title: AIMS Customers – Customer Relationship Management (CRM)
seo.description: Customers, leads, opportunities, sales activities, and every interaction in one record.

products.name: Configure, Price, Quote
products.shortDescription: Product configuration, pricing, quotation generation, and commercial approval workflows for complex offers.
products.definition: CPQ helps sales teams quote complex products correctly and quickly. Valid configurations are guided by rules, prices are calculated from agreed price logic and discounts, and quotations are generated and approved in one flow.
products.problem: Many technical and pricing rules make accurate quotations and discount control complicated.
capabilities: Price lists, discounts, and margin rules
Approval workflows for discounts and terms
Conversion of accepted quotes into orders

distinctions.text: CPQ applies configuration rules and prices the quotation. CRM manages the customer record and the commercial opportunity.

faqs.question: What products suit CPQ?
faqs.answer: Quotations with many options, compatibility rules, complex pricing or discount approvals.

seo.title: AIMS Quote – Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ)
seo.description: Product configuration, pricing, quotation generation, and commercial approval workflows for complex offers.

products.name: B2B Commerce Platform
products.shortDescription: Product catalogues, negotiated pricing, ordering, account management, and order tracking for business customers.
products.definition: The B2B commerce platform lets business customers order from you online the way they actually buy. Each customer sees their own catalogue and prices, places repeat and bulk orders quickly, and follows orders through to delivery.
products.problem: Corporate ordering with contract catalogues and prices is handled across scattered channels.
capabilities: Quick order, bulk order, and reorder
Customer accounts with multiple users and approvals

distinctions.text: B2B commerce is one supplier's sales channel to business customers. A marketplace brings many suppliers and buyers together.

faqs.question: How is B2B commerce different from a public online shop?
faqs.answer: Company accounts, multiple user roles, contract pricing and customer-specific ordering terms are central to it.

seo.title: AIMS Commerce – B2B Commerce Platform (B2B)
seo.description: Product catalogues, negotiated pricing, ordering, account management, and order tracking for business customers.

products.name: B2B Marketplace
products.shortDescription: A digital platform connecting buyers, sellers, and service providers within a market or industry.
products.definition: A B2B marketplace brings the participants of an industry onto one platform. Sellers publish what they offer, buyers discover and request it, and transactions, quotations, and communication happen in one governed place.
products.problem: Buyers and sellers need a shared place to discover supply, compare options and follow their interaction.
capabilities: Product and service listings with search and categories

distinctions.text: A marketplace is multi-sided. B2B commerce is usually one supplier's digital channel to business customers.

faqs.question: Does a marketplace need payment and settlement?
faqs.answer: It depends on the business model. The platform's role, the parties' responsibilities, fees, disputes and settlement need to be settled before design.

seo.title: AIMS Marketplace – B2B Marketplace (B2B)
seo.description: A digital platform connecting buyers, sellers, and service providers within a market or industry.

products.name: Order Management System
products.shortDescription: Track customer orders from submission through processing, fulfilment, delivery, and completion.
products.definition: OMS is the single record of every customer order. It checks availability, orchestrates picking, shipping, and invoicing, and keeps customers and staff informed of the exact status of each order and each line.
products.problem: After an order is placed, supply status, stock allocation, processing and shipping are followed across several separate systems.
capabilities: Order status, splits, backorders, and changes
Fulfilment orchestration with warehouse and transport

distinctions.text: OMS follows order fulfilment. CRM manages the relationship and opportunity before the sale.

faqs.question: How does OMS relate to warehouse stock?
faqs.answer: Allocating orders needs stock data. The authoritative stock source and the update frequency need to be defined.

seo.title: AIMS Orders – Order Management System (OMS)
seo.description: Track customer orders from submission through processing, fulfilment, delivery, and completion.

products.name: Partner and Dealer Management
products.shortDescription: Manage distributors, dealers, resellers, partner information, commercial terms, and channel activity.
products.definition: Partner and Dealer Management gives you a structured view of the sales channel. Partner records, agreements, price terms, targets, and orders are managed together, and partners get a portal to work with you directly.
products.problem: Partner information, territories and channel opportunities are managed without a shared record.
capabilities: Partner and dealer registration and profiles
workflow: Register the partner and channel structure

distinctions.text: Partner management centres on the channel and dealers. CRM usually manages direct customer relationships.

faqs.question: How is partner management different from CRM?
faqs.answer: It focuses on business partners and the sales channel. CRM manages customers and direct opportunities.

seo.title: AIMS Partners – Partner and Dealer Management
seo.description: Manage distributors, dealers, resellers, partner information, commercial terms, and channel activity.

products.name: Customer Portal
products.shortDescription: Give customers access to orders, quotations, invoices, documents, service requests, and account information.
products.definition: The customer portal answers customers' questions without a phone call. They see their orders, quotations, invoices, and documents, raise service requests, and follow progress, while the team handles fewer routine enquiries.
products.problem: Customers depend on repeated contact and file exchange to learn order status or get documents.
workflow: Raise a request or download a document

distinctions.text: The customer portal is a self-service interface. CRM is the internal system for managing customer relationships and activity.

faqs.question: Can a customer see everything?
faqs.answer: No. The portal only shows the data and actions permitted for that account and role.

seo.title: AIMS Portal – Customer Portal
seo.description: Give customers access to orders, quotations, invoices, documents, service requests, and account information.

products.name: Human Capital Management
products.shortDescription: Employee records, organizational structures, recruitment, performance, benefits, and HR processes.
products.definition: HCM is the system of record for people. It holds employee data and organizational structure, supports hiring and development, and routes HR requests and approvals, so HR work is consistent and every change is traceable.
products.problem: Employee records and HR requests are kept in separate tools.
workflow: Register the employee record and org structure

distinctions.text: HCM manages the employee lifecycle. ATS covers recruitment and selection before hiring.

faqs.question: How is HCM different from payroll?
faqs.answer: HCM manages the wider employee lifecycle. Payroll focuses on calculation and payment records.

seo.title: AIMS People – Human Capital Management (HCM)
seo.description: Employee records, organizational structures, recruitment, performance, benefits, and HR processes.

products.name: Applicant Tracking System
products.shortDescription: Recruitment workflows, vacancies, candidates, interviews, and hiring decisions.
products.definition: ATS gives recruitment a clear pipeline. Vacancies are approved and published, candidates are tracked through each stage, interviews are scheduled and scored, and hiring decisions are recorded with their reasons.
products.problem: Résumés, interviews and hiring decisions follow separate paths, so the state of recruitment is unclear.

distinctions.text: ATS covers recruitment through to the hiring decision. HCM manages the employee record and processes after hiring.

faqs.question: Where does an ATS start?
faqs.answer: From defining the need and position and receiving applicants, through assessment to recording the hiring decision.

seo.title: AIMS Talent – Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
seo.description: Recruitment workflows, vacancies, candidates, interviews, and hiring decisions.

products.name: Payroll Management
products.shortDescription: Calculate and manage salaries, deductions, benefits, and payroll records.
products.definition: Payroll turns attendance, contracts, and rules into accurate pay. Calculations are driven by configurable rules, results are reviewed before approval, and every payslip and statutory report is generated from the same verified data.
products.problem: Inconsistencies in attendance data, benefits and deductions make calculation and review of pay difficult.
capabilities: Calculation from attendance, overtime, and leave
Insurance and tax calculations by rule

distinctions.text: Payroll calculates payment. HCM holds the wider employee record and processes.

faqs.question: Are payroll rules the same everywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Components, deductions, tax and legal requirements depend on jurisdiction and the relevant contracts.

seo.title: AIMS Payroll – Payroll Management
seo.description: Calculate and manage salaries, deductions, benefits, and payroll records.

products.name: Workforce Management
products.shortDescription: Shifts, workforce scheduling, attendance, time tracking, and labour allocation.
products.definition: WFM puts the right people in the right place at the right time. Rosters are built against demand and rules, attendance is recorded at source, and labour hours are allocated to the jobs, projects, or cost centres they belong to.
products.problem: If shift plans do not match operational need and actual attendance, covering the work and recording time becomes hard.
capabilities: Attendance through terminals, mobile, or web
Shift swaps and requests with approval

distinctions.text: WFM manages shift schedules and time worked. HCM covers the organisational structure and administrative cycle of people management.

faqs.question: How is WFM different from simple attendance?
faqs.answer: Beyond recording attendance it links shift planning and staff assignment to operational need.

seo.title: AIMS Workforce – Workforce Management (WFM)
seo.description: Shifts, workforce scheduling, attendance, time tracking, and labour allocation.

products.name: Learning Management System
products.shortDescription: Employee training, learning materials, assessments, and certifications.
products.definition: LMS manages how people learn and prove their competence. Courses and materials are delivered online, assessments are scored, and certifications are tracked against role requirements with reminders before they expire.
products.problem: Training and assessment records are scattered, so it is hard to see where each employee stands.
capabilities: Online content and in-person session management
workflow: Enrol or assign a learning path

distinctions.text: LMS manages training and learning records. HCM covers general employee records and HR processes.

faqs.question: Does an LMS issue official certificates?
faqs.answer: It can record completion. The validity of an official certificate depends on the issuing authority.

seo.title: AIMS Learn – Learning Management System (LMS)
seo.description: Employee training, learning materials, assessments, and certifications.

products.name: Enterprise Performance Management
products.shortDescription: Budgeting, financial planning, forecasting, and organizational performance management.
products.definition: EPM connects plans to results. Budgets are built bottom-up with the people who own them, forecasts are refreshed as actuals arrive, and performance indicators show how the organization is tracking against its targets.
products.problem: Budgets and forecasts are prepared in different models and versions, making plan-versus-actual comparison hard.

distinctions.text: EPM covers financial planning and performance. PPM manages selection and governance of the project portfolio.

faqs.question: How is EPM different from ERP?
faqs.answer: ERP records day-to-day transactions. EPM is used for budgeting, forecasting and performance analysis.

seo.title: AIMS Performance – Enterprise Performance Management (EPM)
seo.description: Budgeting, financial planning, forecasting, and organizational performance management.

products.name: Professional Services Automation
products.shortDescription: Project staffing, resource allocation, timesheets, project costs, and service billing.
products.definition: PSA serves organizations that sell expertise and time. It matches people to projects, records the hours they work, tracks project cost and margin, and produces the invoices that follow.
products.problem: In project-based businesses, resource allocation, time recording, cost control and billing stay apart.
capabilities: Project budgets, cost, and margin tracking
Billing rules: fixed price, time and materials, milestones
workflow: Allocate people and plan the work
Report on the project and the basis for billing

distinctions.text: PSA tracks project delivery and service resources. PPM covers selection and prioritisation of the portfolio.

faqs.question: Who is PSA for?
faqs.answer: Project-driven organisations that need to see people's capacity, time, cost and the basis for billing together.

seo.title: AIMS Services – Professional Services Automation (PSA)
seo.description: Project staffing, resource allocation, timesheets, project costs, and service billing.

products.name: IT Service Management
products.shortDescription: Internal IT incidents, service requests, problems, changes, and IT service delivery.
products.definition: ITSM organizes how an IT team serves the rest of the company. Requests and incidents arrive in one queue, are prioritised and resolved against service levels, and changes are reviewed before they touch production.
products.problem: IT requests arrive through different channels, and priority and handling history are inconsistent.
capabilities: Service desk with incident and request queues

distinctions.text: ITSM manages the delivery of IT services. ITAM keeps IT assets and licences.

faqs.question: Is ITSM only for tickets?
faqs.answer: No. Service requests, incidents, problems, changes and the history of handling can all be in scope.

seo.title: AIMS Service Desk – IT Service Management (ITSM)
seo.description: Internal IT incidents, service requests, problems, changes, and IT service delivery.

products.name: IT Asset Management
products.shortDescription: Hardware, software licences, IT inventory, and technology assets under one record.
products.definition: ITAM tells you what technology the organization owns, who uses it, and what it costs. Hardware and licences are tracked from purchase to disposal, so renewals, audits, and refresh planning rely on facts.
products.problem: Without an accurate list of hardware, software and licences, controlling cost and the lifecycle of IT assets is hard.
capabilities: Lifecycle stages from procurement to disposal
workflow: Record the asset and its owner

distinctions.text: ITAM manages IT assets. EAM is broader and covers physical and operational assets.

faqs.question: How is ITAM different from EAM?
faqs.answer: ITAM covers IT assets. EAM is for the organisation's physical and operational assets.

seo.title: AIMS IT Assets – IT Asset Management (ITAM)
seo.description: Hardware, software licences, IT inventory, and technology assets under one record.

products.name: Identity and Access Management
products.shortDescription: Identities, authentication, authorisation, and access policies across all systems.
products.definition: IAM answers who can do what, everywhere. One identity per person connects to all systems, authentication is consistent, and access follows roles and policies that can be reviewed and audited.
products.problem: Accounts and permissions spread across many systems can lead to inconsistent access that is hard to review.
workflow: Take identity from the source of record

distinctions.text: IAM controls identity and access. ITSM manages how IT services are delivered.

faqs.question: What does IAM control?
faqs.answer: It manages the identity lifecycle, authentication and access permissions. Policies need to match roles and the sensitivity of each system.

seo.title: AIMS Access – Identity and Access Management (IAM)
seo.description: Identities, authentication, authorisation, and access policies across all systems.

products.name: Business Process Management
products.shortDescription: Model, automate, monitor, and improve business processes and approval workflows.
products.definition: BPM lets an organization describe how work should flow and then makes it so. Processes are modelled visually, executed with assigned tasks and deadlines, and monitored so bottlenecks show up in data.
products.problem: Business processes depend on email and manual follow-up, and the state of execution and bottlenecks is unclear.

distinctions.text: BPM covers modelling and improving processes. Workflow automation runs a defined path of tasks.

faqs.question: How is BPM different from a simple workflow?
faqs.answer: BPM focuses on modelling and improving a process end to end. A workflow automates the path tasks follow.

seo.title: AIMS Process – Business Process Management (BPM)
seo.description: Model, automate, monitor, and improve business processes and approval workflows.

products.name: Document Management System
products.shortDescription: Store, classify, version, retrieve, and control access to business and technical documents.
products.definition: DMS ends the hunt for the current version. Documents live in one controlled repository with metadata, versions, permissions, and review workflows, so people find the right file quickly and know it is the approved one.
products.problem: Different versions of documents are scattered, and finding the valid one and controlling access is difficult.
capabilities: Central repository with folders and metadata
Access permissions by role and project

distinctions.text: DMS manages documents. ECM manages a wider range of enterprise content.

faqs.question: How is the use of outdated versions prevented?
faqs.answer: Through version control, review and approval status, unique identifiers, and clearly marking the valid version.

seo.title: AIMS Documents – Document Management System (DMS)
seo.description: Store, classify, version, retrieve, and control access to business and technical documents.

products.name: Enterprise Content Management
products.shortDescription: Organizational content and information managed across its whole lifecycle.
products.definition: ECM extends document management to every kind of content the organization produces or receives: scanned paper, email, forms, and reports. It captures, classifies, secures, and retains content under consistent governance.
products.problem: Enterprise content is held in different repositories, and its lifecycle and access are not unified.
capabilities: Capture of scanned, emailed, and digital content
Secure sharing inside and outside the organization
users: Business units handling paper and email

distinctions.text: ECM manages active content. Records management focuses on formal retention and disposition.

faqs.question: How is ECM different from DMS?
faqs.answer: DMS focuses on documents. ECM manages a wider range of enterprise content.

seo.title: AIMS Content – Enterprise Content Management (ECM)
seo.description: Organizational content and information managed across its whole lifecycle.

products.name: Governance, Risk and Compliance
products.shortDescription: Risk management, internal controls, compliance obligations, and governance activities.
products.definition: GRC gives one view of what could go wrong and how it is being controlled. Risks, controls, policies, and obligations are registered, owned, tested, and reported, so the organization can show that it governs itself.
products.problem: Risks, controls and evidence are spread across departments, making it hard to monitor obligations.
capabilities: Risk register with assessment and treatment

distinctions.text: GRC coordinates the risk and control framework. Audit management covers running tests and following findings.

faqs.question: Does GRC replace internal audit?
faqs.answer: No. GRC coordinates the risk and compliance framework. Audit is one of the assessment mechanisms.

seo.title: AIMS Compliance – Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC)
seo.description: Risk management, internal controls, compliance obligations, and governance activities.

products.name: Audit Management
products.shortDescription: Plan audits and track findings, evidence, corrective actions, and audit status.
products.definition: Audit Management runs the audit cycle from annual plan to closed finding. Audits are scheduled, checklists executed, evidence attached, and findings followed up until the corrective action is verified.
products.problem: Planning audits and following evidence and findings through separate files limits transparency.

distinctions.text: Audit management is a tool for planning and follow-up. GRC has a wider scope of risk and control.

faqs.question: Does audit management software perform the audit?
faqs.answer: No. It organises the plan, evidence and actions. Professional judgement stays with the auditors.

seo.title: AIMS Audit – Audit Management
seo.description: Plan audits and track findings, evidence, corrective actions, and audit status.

products.name: Case Management
products.shortDescription: Structured cases, investigations, complaints, and requests with their workflows and history.
products.definition: Case Management handles work that does not follow a fixed path: complaints, claims, investigations, and special requests. Each case collects its documents, tasks, and decisions in one record and moves through a flexible workflow.
products.problem: Handling a request or complaint without a single ID, owner and history leads to inconsistency.
capabilities: Case intake from forms, email, and portals
Flexible workflows with ad hoc tasks
Documents, notes, and decisions on each case
Case types with their own fields and rules

distinctions.text: Case management centres on an individual case. BPM models the general flow of processes.

faqs.question: What is case management used for?
faqs.answer: Matters that each have their own ID, owner, stages, documents and outcome, such as a complaint or a request.

seo.title: AIMS Cases – Case Management
seo.description: Structured cases, investigations, complaints, and requests with their workflows and history.

products.name: Records Management
products.shortDescription: Business records, retention schedules, archiving, and disposition under enforced rules.
products.definition: Records Management makes retention policy operational. Each record has a class, a retention period, and an owner, and the system moves it to archive or disposition on schedule, with an audit trail of what was done and why.
products.problem: Keeping records without classification and a retention period makes retrieval and authorised disposal difficult.
capabilities: Search and retrieval of archived records
workflow: Move to archive or hold disposal

distinctions.text: Records management focuses on retention periods and formal disposition. DMS covers registering and retrieving documents.

faqs.question: When does a document become an organisational record?
faqs.answer: When it has evidential or administrative value under approved policy and its retention and disposition are defined.

seo.title: AIMS Records – Records Management
seo.description: Business records, retention schedules, archiving, and disposition under enforced rules.

products.name: Enterprise Workflow Automation
products.shortDescription: Reusable workflow, rules, task routing, notifications, deadlines, and escalation across business functions.
products.definition: Workflow Automation is the shared engine that moves work between people and systems. Approvals, notifications, and escalations are defined once as rules and reused in every product, which is what keeps customisation inexpensive and consistent.
products.problem: Repeated approvals and manual hand-offs leave responsibility and status of work unclear.
capabilities: Notifications by email and messaging channels
Triggers from events in other systems

distinctions.text: Workflow automation runs the tasks on a defined path. BPM suits modelling and improving the whole process.

faqs.question: Does workflow automation need a full redesign?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A single clear path can be automated. End-to-end process redesign belongs to BPM.

seo.title: AIMS Flow – Enterprise Workflow Automation
seo.description: Reusable workflow, rules, task routing, notifications, deadlines, and escalation across business functions.

products.name: Project Portfolio Management
products.shortDescription: Projects, budgets, resources, schedules, and organizational project portfolios.
products.definition: PPM lets management see all projects together. Schedules, budgets, risks, and resource demand are tracked per project and rolled up to the portfolio, so priorities and trade-offs are decided on a complete picture.
products.problem: Choosing projects without comparing value, cost, capacity and dependencies can spread resources thin.
capabilities: Project registers with stages and gates

distinctions.text: PPM manages selection and priorities of the portfolio. PSA follows project execution and resources.

faqs.question: How is PPM different from managing one project?
faqs.answer: Project management focuses on delivering one project. PPM looks at the set of projects in terms of priority and resources.

seo.title: AIMS Portfolio – Project Portfolio Management (PPM)
seo.description: Projects, budgets, resources, schedules, and organizational project portfolios.

products.name: Facilities Management
products.shortDescription: Buildings, infrastructure, services, and the operational activities that keep them running.
products.definition: Facilities Management covers the buildings and services an organization runs on. Spaces, equipment, service contracts, and requests are managed in one place so occupants get responsive service and managers see the cost of running each site.
products.problem: Building service and repair requests are followed without a shared picture of the site and its assets.
workflow: Assign work to a team or contractor

distinctions.text: Facilities management focuses on buildings, space and workplace services. EAM covers the lifecycle of a wider range of physical assets.

faqs.question: How is facilities management different from EAM?
faqs.answer: Facilities management focuses on buildings, space and workplace services. EAM covers a wider range of assets.

seo.title: AIMS Facilities – Facilities Management
seo.description: Buildings, infrastructure, services, and the operational activities that keep them running.

products.name: Business Intelligence
products.shortDescription: Reporting, dashboards, performance indicators, and analytical insight from business data.
products.definition: BI puts the numbers in front of the people who decide. Data from the company's systems is modelled into consistent measures, and dashboards and reports let managers see current performance and drill into the reasons behind it.
products.problem: Many reports with different indicator definitions do not give one consistent view of performance.

distinctions.text: BI is the analysis and presentation layer. A data warehouse holds the modelled historical data it draws on.

faqs.question: Does BI guarantee data quality?
faqs.answer: No. Report quality depends on the source, indicator definitions, transformation rules and data governance.

seo.title: AIMS Insight – Business Intelligence (BI)
seo.description: Reporting, dashboards, performance indicators, and analytical insight from business data.

products.name: Industrial Analytics
products.shortDescription: Analysis of production, process, maintenance, quality, energy, and equipment data.
products.definition: Industrial Analytics combines data that plants usually keep apart: production, process readings, maintenance, quality, and energy. Analysing them together shows what actually drives yield, downtime, and cost.
products.problem: Production, quality, maintenance and energy data are analysed separately, so cause and effect are hard to see.
capabilities: Combined analysis of process, quality, and maintenance data

distinctions.text: Industrial analytics works on plant data and operational questions. BI covers management reporting across the organisation.

faqs.question: How is industrial analytics different from BI?
faqs.answer: It studies process, machine and production data in operational context. BI has a broader organisational scope.

seo.title: AIMS Analytics – Industrial Analytics
seo.description: Analysis of production, process, maintenance, quality, energy, and equipment data.

products.name: Data Integration Platform
products.shortDescription: Connect applications and data sources through APIs, events, scheduled exchanges, and integration workflows.
products.definition: The integration platform makes systems talk to each other without custom point-to-point code. Connectors, transformations, and flows are configured and monitored in one place, so data moves once and arrives reliably.
products.problem: Point-to-point links and manual exchange make data flows hard to maintain and errors hard to manage.
capabilities: Connectors for APIs, databases, files, and messaging

distinctions.text: iPaaS coordinates the flow of data between systems. An operational data platform gives operational data context and serves it.

faqs.question: Does iPaaS guarantee a connection to any system?
faqs.answer: No. Whether a connection is possible depends on the API, protocol, access and data structure of both ends.

seo.title: AIMS Integrate – Data Integration Platform (iPaaS)
seo.description: Connect applications and data sources through APIs, events, scheduled exchanges, and integration workflows.

products.name: Master Data Management
products.shortDescription: Consistent, governed master data for products, assets, suppliers, customers, and locations.
products.definition: MDM gives each business entity a single, trusted record. Products, suppliers, customers, assets, and locations are defined once, cleansed, approved, and shared with every system that needs them, ending conflicting copies.
products.problem: Duplicate and inconsistent records for products, customers and suppliers build up across systems.
capabilities: Golden records for key business entities
Approval workflows for creation and change
Distribution of master data to other systems
workflow: Define the entity and the source of record

distinctions.text: MDM manages current reference data. A data warehouse holds historical and analytical data.

faqs.question: How does MDM deal with duplicate data?
faqs.answer: Matching and quality rules identify similar records, and merging or approval follows data ownership.

seo.title: AIMS Master Data – Master Data Management (MDM)
seo.description: Consistent, governed master data for products, assets, suppliers, customers, and locations.

products.name: Digital Twin Platform
products.shortDescription: Digital representations of physical assets, facilities, or processes built from engineering and operational data.
products.definition: A digital twin ties a physical asset to everything known about it. Structure, documents, live readings, and maintenance history are shown together in a web view, so engineers and operators work from one model of the facility.
products.problem: Engineering models, condition and asset history sit in separate sources, so no contextual picture forms.
capabilities: Asset and facility models with relationships
Live and historical readings on the model
Maintenance and inspection history per component
Scenario and what-if calculations where models exist
workflow: Define the asset and its component structure

distinctions.text: A digital twin organises data and models around a specific asset or process. An operational data platform is a more general data layer.

faqs.question: Does a digital twin have to be 3D?
faqs.answer: No. It can be a structural or schematic, data-driven model. The level of representation should match the purpose and the available data.

seo.title: AIMS Twin – Digital Twin Platform
seo.description: Digital representations of physical assets, facilities, or processes built from engineering and operational data.

products.name: Operational Data Platform
products.shortDescription: Collect, organise, and expose operational data for reporting, monitoring, and integration.
products.definition: The operational data platform is the shared data layer beneath operations. It brings together readings, events, and transactional data from plant and business systems, gives them a consistent structure, and offers them to dashboards, analytics, and other applications through governed interfaces.
products.problem: Operational data comes in different formats and timings from different sources and is hard to reuse.
capabilities: Ingestion from equipment, historians, and business systems
Common data model for assets, events, and measurements
APIs and query services for applications

distinctions.text: An operational data platform adds context to several types of operational data. A historian is more specialised for industrial time-series data.

faqs.question: How does an ODP differ from a data warehouse?
faqs.answer: An ODP focuses on operational data and its use by applications. A warehouse usually holds analytical history and the reporting model.

seo.title: AIMS Data – Operational Data Platform
seo.description: Collect, organise, and expose operational data for reporting, monitoring, and integration.

products.name: OEE and Production Performance
products.shortDescription: Measure availability, performance, and quality to expose manufacturing losses and improvement opportunities.
products.definition: OEE turns production data into a clear measure of how well equipment is used. Losses are captured with their reasons and ranked, so improvement effort goes to the stoppages, slow cycles, and defects that cost the most.
products.problem: Recording stoppages and speed loss without a shared definition does not show how much each factor costs in lost output.
capabilities: OEE calculation by machine, line, and shift
Live production boards for the floor

distinctions.text: OEE analyses indicators and causes of loss. MES records order execution and production events.

faqs.question: Does OEE alone identify the cause of a stoppage?
faqs.answer: No. OEE measures how much is lost. Reason codes and further analysis are needed to find the root cause.

seo.title: AIMS Efficiency – OEE and Production Performance (OEE)
seo.description: Measure availability, performance, and quality to expose manufacturing losses and improvement opportunities.

products.name: Data Warehouse
products.shortDescription: Centralised storage and organisation of data for analysis and reporting.
products.definition: The data warehouse is where history lives. Data from many systems is loaded, cleaned, and modelled around business subjects, so reports run fast, definitions agree, and the operational systems are not burdened by analytical queries.
products.problem: Reporting directly from operational systems scatters history and data definitions and adds query load.
capabilities: Scheduled and incremental loading from source systems
Query services for reporting and analytics

distinctions.text: A data warehouse holds modelled historical data. BI uses it for indicators, reports and dashboards.

faqs.question: Why not report directly from the ERP?
faqs.answer: For simple reporting that may be enough. A warehouse becomes relevant when history and combining several sources matter.

seo.title: AIMS Data Warehouse – Data Warehouse (DWH)
seo.description: Centralised storage and organisation of data for analysis and reporting.

products.name: Process Mining
products.shortDescription: Analyse how business processes really run from event data, to find inefficiencies and deviations.
products.definition: Process Mining reconstructs real process flows from the timestamps systems already record. It shows how orders, requests, and approvals actually move, where they wait, and where they leave the intended path.
products.problem: The real path a process takes can differ from the designed model, leaving bottlenecks hidden.

distinctions.text: Process mining discovers the real path from events. BPM models the target process and manages execution.

faqs.question: What data does process mining need?
faqs.answer: At minimum a case ID, an activity name and the time of each event. Coverage and data quality determine how reliable the analysis is.

seo.title: AIMS Discover – Process Mining
seo.description: Analyse how business processes really run from event data, to find inefficiencies and deviations.

industries.name: Manufacturing
industries.summary: Software for discrete and process manufacturing, production planning, quality, maintenance, materials and traceability.
industries.overview: In manufacturing, a customer order has to become a plan for materials, capacity, operations, quality control and delivery. The type of production, discrete or process, shapes the product structure, routing, consumption records, traceability and quality control. Information systems help when they connect engineering, planning and shop-floor data.

subsectors.name: Discrete Manufacturing
subsectors.description: Products built from parts and assemblies in defined stages. Product structure, routing and part traceability matter.

subsectors.name: Process Manufacturing
subsectors.description: Production based on formulas, material mixes, process parameters and batches. Control of variables and traceability of materials matter.

subsectors.name: Polymer & Plastics
subsectors.description: Processes such as compounding, extrusion and injection moulding. Formulas, raw materials, machine parameters and product quality matter.

subsectors.name: Forging
subsectors.description: Parts made by deforming metal. Material traceability, heat treatment, process stages and inspection matter.

subsectors.name: Foundry
subsectors.description: Parts made by melting and casting. Control of the melt, moulds, material composition and testing matter.

processes: Order and line-capacity planning
Supply of materials, parts and consumables
Production execution, operation records and batch traceability
Incoming, in-process and final quality control
Equipment maintenance and downtime management
Storage, packing and dispatch
challenges: Aligning the production plan with real capacity and material availability
Tracing raw materials through batch to finished product
Recording the cause of stoppages, scrap and rework in a form that can be analysed
Keeping drawing versions, formulas and work instructions aligned with production
Linking quality and laboratory results to the right order and batch
integration: Linking orders and the production plan in ERP and APS with execution records in MES
Linking machine and sensor data to a historian and an operational data platform
Linking inspection and test records to QMS and LIMS
Keeping material, part and product identifiers consistent across PLM, ERP and WMS

faqs.question: Do discrete and process manufacturing need the same software model?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Product structure, routing, formulas and traceability differ between the two, so the scope of the system should match the kind of production.

faqs.question: Which system should we start with?
faqs.answer: It depends on the main problem. Production planning and execution, maintenance, quality, warehousing and enterprise resource coordination each suggest a different starting point.

solutions.name: Maintenance and Reliability
solutions.summary: Plan, execute, and learn from maintenance work so equipment stays available and repair costs stay predictable.
solutions.problem: Maintenance often runs on paper, memory, and urgency. Requests get lost, preventive work slips, spare parts run out at the wrong moment, and nobody can say which machines cost the most to keep running.
outcomes: Every request, work order, and inspection recorded against the asset it concerns
Preventive schedules driven by time, counters, or condition instead of habit
Spare parts linked to work orders and reordered before they run out
Maintenance history that shows recurring failures and real cost per asset
integration: The asset and location structure must be valid.
Failure codes and causes of stoppage need to be defined.
Spare-parts stock and repair records should be tied to the work order.

faqs.question: Are preventive and predictive maintenance the same?
faqs.answer: No. Preventive maintenance relies on a schedule or trigger set in advance. Predictive maintenance uses condition data and analysis to estimate when or how likely action is needed.

solutions.name: Asset Management
solutions.summary: Keep a trustworthy record of physical and IT assets from acquisition through operation to retirement.
solutions.problem: Asset information is scattered across spreadsheets, drawings, and people's heads. Without one authoritative record, it is hard to plan renewals, justify budgets, prove compliance, or know what you actually own.
outcomes: One hierarchical register of plants, systems, equipment, and components
Lifecycle history from purchase to disposal for every asset
Condition and performance data that supports renewal and budget decisions
Hardware and software inventories under the same governance as plant assets
integration: Asset identifiers and hierarchy must be consistent.
Cost and repair history should be linked to the asset.
IT assets should be kept separate from physical operational assets.

faqs.question: What should be listed to start with asset management?
faqs.answer: Identifier, location, specification, criticality, ownership and the main history of each asset. The level of detail should fit the decisions the organisation wants to support.

seo.title: Asset Management

solutions.name: Procurement and Sourcing
solutions.summary: Run the full buying cycle, from requisition and supplier selection to contract, order, and delivery.
solutions.problem: Purchasing is a chain of handoffs: requisitions, quotations, comparisons, approvals, contracts, and orders. When each step lives in a different inbox, nothing is comparable, nothing is auditable, and good suppliers are hard to tell from convenient ones.
outcomes: Requisitions approved against policy and budget before anything is bought
Quotation requests sent to qualified suppliers and answers compared side by side
Award decisions recorded with their reasons
Orders, deliveries, and supplier performance tracked in one chain
integration: Purchase categories and approval authority need to be defined.
Technical specifications and commercial terms must be comparable.
The supplier ID should be the same across related systems.

faqs.question: Does every purchase need a formal sourcing event?
faqs.answer: No. The type of purchase, its value, risk, urgency and company policy decide whether a request goes through simple purchasing, a quotation request or formal competition.

solutions.name: Sales and Customer Management

Configured, correctly priced quotations generated and approved quickly
Orders tracked from submission to delivery
Customers and partners served through their own portals

Price and discount rules need approval from the commercial owner.
Passing data from opportunity to order should not create duplicates.

faqs.question: Does CRM replace the order system?

solutions.name: Production Planning and Execution
solutions.summary: Connect planning, scheduling, shop-floor execution, and performance measurement into one production flow.
solutions.problem: Plans made in the office rarely survive contact with the shop floor. When production orders, materials, and actual results live in different places, delays surface late, losses go unmeasured, and traceability is reconstructed by hand.
outcomes: Production orders scheduled against real capacity, materials, and constraints
Shop-floor activity, batches, and materials recorded as work happens
Availability, performance, and quality losses measured and visible
Full traceability from raw material to finished product
integration: Product structure and routing must be valid.
Capacity and operation times should be updated to match reality.
Shop-floor data capture needs a defined source and owner.

faqs.question: What data is basic to production planning and execution?
faqs.answer: Product structure, routing, work centres, capacity calendar, materials, operation times and the order ID.
