solutions.name: Quality and Laboratory
solutions.summary: Control inspections, laboratory testing, non-conformities, and corrective actions with complete records.
solutions.problem: Quality depends on records that are complete, consistent, and retrievable years later. Paper logs and separate laboratory files make it hard to trace a result to a sample, a batch, or a corrective action.
outcomes: Inspection plans and laboratory tests executed and recorded in one system
Samples traced to requests, methods, instruments, and results
Non-conformities handled through corrective and preventive actions
Audit-ready quality records, retrievable in seconds
integration: Acceptance limits and the sampling method need to be approved.
Sample and product IDs must be traceable.
Test-method versions and review records need to be controlled.

faqs.question: Do QMS and LIMS need to be connected?
faqs.answer: If laboratory results feed quality decisions, linking the sample ID, method, result and non-conformance can be essential. How to connect depends on the existing systems.

seo.title: Quality and Laboratory

solutions.name: Inventory, Warehouse and Logistics
solutions.summary: Know what you hold, where it is, and how it moves, from receiving through storage to dispatch and transport.
solutions.problem: Stock counts that disagree with reality cause stoppages, over-ordering, and slow dispatch. When warehouse movements, purchasing, and transport are tracked separately, no one has a reliable picture of availability.
outcomes: Accurate stock by location, batch, and status
Receiving, put-away, picking, and dispatch handled as controlled movements
Shipments, carriers, and transport costs planned and tracked
Replenishment triggered by actual consumption and lead times
integration: Item IDs and packaging units must be consistent.
Stock status and reservation rules need to be defined.
The boundary between warehouse stock and order status should be clear.

faqs.question: Is a WMS needed if we already have an ERP?
faqs.answer: An ERP records stock at an overall level. A WMS adds location, movement and handling detail inside the warehouse. Whether it is needed depends on how complex warehouse operations are.

seo.title: Inventory, Warehouse and Logistics

solutions.name: Safety and Environment
solutions.summary: Manage incidents, inspections, risk assessments, work authorisation, and environmental obligations.
solutions.problem: Safety and environmental management is only as good as its follow-through. Incidents are reported late, inspections are not closed out, and permits and risk assessments sit in files that no one can search.
outcomes: Incidents and near-misses reported quickly, with investigation and action tracking
Inspections and risk assessments scheduled and closed out
Hazardous work controlled through permit and authorisation workflows
Environmental data and compliance reporting prepared from live records

The roles of issuer, approver and performer should be kept separate.
Recording incidents and actions should be timely and traceable.

faqs.question: Does a work-permit workflow alone ensure safe work?
faqs.answer: No. The system can organise recording and approval of the steps. Field assessment, competence of people and carrying out the real controls are still essential.

Shifts, attendance, and labour allocation planned and recorded
Payroll calculated from consistent source data
Training and certifications tracked against role requirements

faqs.question: Should attendance data be kept in HCM?

solutions.name: Finance and Planning
solutions.summary: Connect accounting, budgets, spend, projects, and forecasts so financial decisions rest on live operational data.
solutions.problem: Finance often sees operations through monthly exports. Budgets are set in one file, spend is tracked in another, and project costs arrive late, so corrective decisions are made after the money is gone.
outcomes: Accounting, purchasing, inventory, and sales linked in one ledger of record
Budgets and forecasts compared with actuals continuously
Spend visible by category, supplier, and cost centre
Project cost, timesheets, and billing tied to the same data
integration: Financial dimensions and the reporting calendar should be the same.
The version and owner of assumptions need to be recorded.
The source of actual data should be separate from the planning model.

faqs.question: Why does the version of budget assumptions matter?
faqs.answer: Because comparing scenarios with actual performance only makes sense when the basis of calculation, the date of each change and the owner of each assumption can be traced.

seo.title: Finance and Planning

solutions.name: Process Automation and Integration
solutions.summary: Automate approvals and workflows, handle service requests and cases, and connect systems so data moves once.
solutions.problem: Approvals by email and re-keying between systems waste time and hide errors. Every manual handoff is a place where work stalls, and every disconnected system is a place where data disagrees.
outcomes: Approval and routing rules modelled once and reused across functions
Deadlines, escalations, and notifications handled automatically
Requests, incidents, and cases tracked to resolution
Systems connected through APIs and events instead of manual re-entry
integration: The process owner and the source system must be identified.
Error handling and repeatability of exchanges matter.
Access and event logging should fit the sensitivity of the data.

faqs.question: When should the process be redesigned first?
faqs.answer: When ownership, steps, exceptions or decision rules are unclear, automating too early can lock in existing complexity. The process should be understood and simplified first.

solutions.name: Data, Analytics and Intelligence
solutions.summary: Turn operational and business data into dashboards, monitoring, forecasts, and decision support.
solutions.problem: Data exists in abundance but is hard to use: different systems define the same thing differently, reports are built by hand, and signals from equipment reach decision-makers too late to matter.

Dashboards and indicators that managers can trust and drill into
Real-time monitoring of equipment and operations
Forecasts and models that support planning and maintenance decisions

Quality, timestamp and origin of the data need checking.
Correlation alone does not prove cause and effect.

faqs.question: Does a dashboard on its own improve decisions?
faqs.answer: No. An indicator needs a clear definition, a reliable source, an update frequency and an owner, and it should answer a specific decision question.

solutions.name: Governance, Risk and Compliance

outcomes: Risks and internal controls registered, owned, and reviewed
Audits planned with findings, evidence, and corrective actions tracked
Contracts managed from drafting through renewal and expiry
Identities, roles, and access policies governed centrally

Ownership of controls and evidence should be clear.
The system does not replace legal or professional judgement.

faqs.question: Does GRC guarantee legal compliance?
faqs.answer: No. The system can organise requirements, controls and evidence. Interpreting regulations and confirming compliance remain with the responsible people and specialists.

seo.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance

Document review and approval handled as workflow
Records retained, archived, and disposed of by schedule
Engineering documents and revisions linked to products and assets

Retention and disposal periods need an approved policy.

faqs.question: Must every document be kept as a record?
faqs.answer: No. The type of document, its administrative or evidential value and the retention policy decide what is an official record and what is working content or a current document.

platform.lead: Each system has a clear job. Where processes cross, we connect them deliberately, with the data and the owners agreed in advance.

sections.title: Cloud or on-premise
sections.text: Systems can run as a hosted service or on servers you control. The choice follows your security policy, network and who will operate the system day to day.

sections.title: Integration by design
sections.text: Systems exchange data through APIs, files, databases or equipment protocols. Each connection is designed around its source and target, then tested and documented.

sections.title: Roles and access

sections.title: Data you can use
sections.text: We document the data model and agree on export formats at the start, so your information stays usable beyond any single system.

sections.title: Operations
sections.text: Monitoring, backup, updates and support arrangements are agreed for each deployment, not assumed.

seo.title: How we work
seo.description: Our engagement approach: understand the process, define scope, configure or build, integrate, deploy and support.

how.title: From your process to a working system
how.lead: A clear sequence, agreed scope at each step, and your people involved throughout.

steps.title: Understand the operation
steps.text: We learn how the work really runs: processes, roles, assets, paperwork and the systems already in use.

steps.title: Define scope and architecture
steps.text: Together we agree what the system covers, who uses it, which data it holds and how it connects to what exists.

steps.title: Configure or build
steps.text: We shape modules, forms, workflows and reports to your process, showing progress in working increments.

steps.title: Integrate and test
steps.text: We connect the system to your other software and data sources and test it with your real scenarios.

steps.title: Deploy and train
steps.text: We install it in the cloud or on your servers, migrate the data that matters and train the people who will use it.

steps.title: Support and improve
steps.text: After launch we keep supporting the system and refine it as your process changes.
